fields.sample_size: 100 residents of Kanyama township, Lusaka (simple random sampling; Yamane formula n = 400,170 / [1 + 400,170 x 0.10^2] = 100 at 90% confidence and 10% error; age 15-49, 40% aged 15-24; 50% female); questionnaires with open and closed questions plus key-informant and in-depth interviews and a desk review; September-November 2024
fields.effect_measure: descriptive percentages and frequencies (SPSS and Excel); no inferential statistics
fields.effect_estimate: 70% of respondents rely on municipal tap water and 30% on hand-dug wells; 70% have no alternative source; 60% believe the water quality is good; 55% report water scarcity and 70% face difficulty accessing water at least weekly (30% daily); 70% collect water in under 30 minutes; 50% pay for water and 70% of payers say the payment is unfair; 65% are willing to pay for better access; 80% have a family toilet (62.5% private, 37.5% shared); rating of water availability 40% good, 35% fair, 25% poor; 45% attribute scarcity to climate change; 50% store water in large closed tanks and 40% in small covered containers. The authors conclude that residents depend on an intermittent municipal supply with no alternatives, that governance is ineffective and infrastructure sub-standard, and call for a multi-sectoral approach; limitations: self-reported data, cross-sectional, language barriers, medium response rate.
fields.section: Full text (10 pages): Materials and methods (study design, sampling, Yamane formula); Results (Tables 1-4, Figures 2-7); Discussion; Study limitations
fields.exact_location: Sampling section (n = 100); Table 2 (water availability, quality, accessibility); Table 4 (water security perceptions); Acque Sotterranee 14(4):41-50

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods survey of 100 residents of Kanyama township, Lusaka, on water security and climate vulnerability; read in full text 2026-10-04. Percentages and frequencies only; the legal and governance content is thin (the abstract mentions weak enforcement and ineffective governance).
